Eli (NovaSearch): Hey @support, our monthly invoice suddenly jumped ~5x after we switched from embeddings.batch -> rerank.batch. Dashboard still shows ~10k inputs but invoice charged like 50k embedding units. Can someone help dig in? We didn't change traffic.

Jen S (Support): hey @Eli — sorry to hear that. Can you paste a sample request payload and SDK version? also your project id / org id (or pm me in DMs).

Eli (NovaSearch): thanks Jen. SDK: redwood-js 0.9.2. Project: nova-prod-01. Sample payload (redacted keys):
```
POST /v1/rerank.batch
Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED
{
  "model": "open-embed-1536",
  "queries": ["search query 1", "search query 2"],
  "candidates": [
    ["doc1 text...", "doc2 text...", ... up to 100 per query]
  ],
  "rerank_type": "pairwise",
  "batch": true
}
```
We send ~100 candidates per query and 100 queries in the batch (so 10k comparisons theoretically). Dashboard shows "inputs: 10k" but invoice line item shows 1,000,000 embedding units with dimensions=1536, which feels like pairwise got expanded wrong.

Mike R (Eng-Inference): @Jen / @Eli — quick clarifying q: when you say "embedding units" do you mean the invoice line says "embeddings (open-embed-1536) — 1,536,000 units"?

Eli (NovaSearch): yes exactly. It lists embeddings.open-embed-1536 1,536,000 units across that billing window.

Jen S (Support): ok filing incident to eng. @billing Sam B can you pull that invoice line and show meter events for nova-prod-01 for the window 2026-02-15 -> 2026-03-15?

Sam B (Billing): pulling now. I see invoice #INV-2026-1854 charged embeddings.open-embed-1536 = 1,536,000 units. Metering events show many events with metric "embedding_vector_units" and a pattern of repeated counts during rerank.batch calls from that project. I'll attach a CSV to the ticket.

Mike R (Eng-Inference): @Eli can you run a minimal repro script? ideally:
- single query with 3 candidates
- rerank_type: pairwise
- batch size 1
and paste the raw request/response and the meter log snippet from the server (if available).

Eli (NovaSearch): repro attached. I ran locally against staging with a small payload:
```
POST /v1/rerank.batch
{
  "model":"open-embed-1536",
  "queries":["q1"],
  "candidates":[["a","b","c"]],
  "rerank_type":"pairwise"
}
```
Response ok. Metering line returned in headers: `x-redwood-metering: event=embeddings_request;inputs=3;pairwise=true;reported_units=9;dims=1536`

Jen S (Support): interesting header. @Mike R does `reported_units=9` look right? (pairwise of 3 candidates -> 3 choose 2 = 3 comparisons, not 9)

Mike R (Eng-Inference): aha. That header is wrong. Our pairwise accounting currently multiplies inputs * candidates instead of choosing nC2 for pairwise cross-encoder calls when the caller uses the batch matrix path. For a single query with 3 candidates we should have 3 pairwise compares (3), not 9. So a bug in the metering logic leads to overcounting by factor ~= num_candidates for batched queries.

Mike R (Eng-Inference): reproduction steps I ran on prod-sim show the same: for Q queries with C candidates per query, we currently record units ~= Q * C * C instead of Q * (C choose 2) in the pairwise path. The bug is in metering/cost_estimator.py line ~214 where we use `comparisons = inputs * candidates_count` when pairwise flag is true. Fix is to compute `comparisons = inputs * (candidates_count * (candidates_count - 1) / 2)`.

Jen S (Support): thanks @Mike. @Eli we will issue a billing credit for the measured overcharge while we patch. Can you confirm the date range and approximate amount you were charged extra? We'll estimate and then billing will post a credit.

Eli (NovaSearch): charged extra between 2026-02-10 and 2026-03-10. Invoices show an extra ~1,200,000 units. Estimate USD ~$600.

Sam B (Billing): noted. I'll provisionally credit $600 to nova-prod-01 pending exact meter reconciliation. ETA 3 business days.

Mike R (Eng-Inference): action plan:
- patch metering to use nC2 for pairwise (PR open: github.com/redwood/inference@pr/4821)
- add unit tests for pairwise vs pointwise batch combos
- backfill corrected meter events for affected window (script under infra/metering/backfill_pairwise.py)
- postmortem and alert to detect similar regressions

Mike R (Eng-Inference): temporary mitigation: for customers using rerank.pairwise, recommend sending smaller candidate sets or switching to `rerank_type: pointwise` if pairwise semantics not required until patch is live.

Jen S (Support): @Eli I'll DM you the ticket link and the provisional credit details. We'll follow up when PR is deployed. Thanks for the clear repro — that sped root cause.

Eli (NovaSearch): thanks all. Appreciate the quick triage. One ask: can you log the SDK version somewhere so we know if older clients trigger the bad path? We used redwood-js 0.9.2.

Mike R (Eng-Inference): noted — the bad branch is triggered by batched pairwise requests that use the matrix scoring kernel; we'll add telemetry to include SDK version and request features in the meter event. That should help detect if older SDKs need client-side mitigation.

deploy-bot: Deployment started: eng/pr/4821 -> staging

Mike R (Eng-Inference): deployed patch to staging, running tests. Will schedule deploy to prod in next maintenance window. I'll follow up with backfill timeline.

Sam B (Billing): credit issued: $600 provisional to customer account nova-prod-01. Final adjust pending backfill.

Eli (NovaSearch): confirmed credit received. Leaving thread open until backfill done. :thumbsup:

Jen S (Support): keeping open. Closing once backfill and final billing reconciliation complete. Thanks everyone.
